title: Visionära samtal i fokus på Kulturpolitisk samling 2026
content:
Den 12 oktober bjuder Svensk Scenkonst och Sveriges Museer in till tredje upplagan av Kulturpolitisk samling, där en rad aktörer i samhället möts kring en aktuell och utvald fråga för kulturlivet. Årets forum är en visionsdag om Sverige som kulturland och framtidens kulturpolitik.

Evenemanget hålls på Kulturhuset Stadsteatern och livesänds i Svensk Scenkonsts och Sveriges Museers Youtubekanaler. 

Årets tema, ”Kulturriket Sverige”, handlar om vilken kulturpolitik Sverige behöver idag och framåt.

– Det behövs en ny och brett förankrad vision om vilket kulturland Sverige ska vara. Vi vill se ett land där konst, kultur och bildning är en självklar del av samhällsbygget och där kulturens kraft tas tillvara för att möta framtidens utmaningar. Med Kulturpolitisk samling vill vi öppna för samtal om hur en ny kulturpolitik kan se ut, säger Mikael Brännvall, vd för Svensk Scenkonst.

Begreppet Kulturriket Sverige ska inte ses som en färdig politisk modell. Målet med dagen är i stället att samla en rad aktörer och tillsammans börja formulera de frågor och den riktning som en ny kulturpolitik behöver ta sin utgångspunkt i.

title: Read the charter for the White House’s ‘Super Intelligence Force’
content:
The Trump administration has given its newly created “Super Intelligence Force” broad authority to determine how the tech industry and the federal government should address threats to national security and civil liberties posed by fast-evolving artificial intelligence technology, according to a charter obtained by POLITICO.

Three people familiar with discussions about the task force confirmed the document’s authenticity. The people were granted anonymity to share details that are not yet public.

The task force will identify “measures to improve the preparedness and response capability of both the government and the private sector to threats to the homeland and the American people,” the charter states. It will also produce a report on the risks of AI, focusing on “potential threats to civil liberties,” cybersecurity, standards for advanced models, and the impacts of possible overregulation.

The Wall Street Journal first reported on the details of the charter.

title: Google told to halt work on datacentres in Finland over environmental concerns
content:
Order on two construction sites comes after Google failed to carry out environmental impact assessments

Google has been ordered to temporarily stop work on two datacentres in Finland after failing to carry out the necessary environmental impact assessments on its construction sites.

The planned datacentres in Muhos and Kajanni are part of a €13bn (£11bn) project across multiple sites in northern Finland by the technology company amid huge demand for space to house online infrastructure.

title: Spain’s snap election: will Pedro Sánchez’s latest gamble pay off?
content:
On October 5, Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap general election for November 29, bringing the vote forward by 10 months.

One of the main advantages of being in government is the ability to shape the political agenda. Spain’s system also grants incumbent leaders the power to call (or not call) early elections. So why is Sánchez calling elections now?

On the face of it, it seems like like odd timing, as Sánchez’s Socialist party (the PSOE) and the government it leads have been under intense pressure for months.

The inner circles of both the PSOE and Sánchez himself have been dogged by years of corruption allegations. The crisis in Ceuta has added further pressure – it shifted the migration debate towards security and deportations, and away from Sánchez’s position of regularisation, employment and inclusion.

But recent events have placed housing front and centre. The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal – a disabled 87-year-old in Madrid whose rent was hiked by 230% after an investment fund bought her house – sparked protests across Spain, including encampments in major city centres.

title: How geopolitical tensions tainted the 2026 Asian Games
content:
The 2026 Asian Games in Japan drew to a close on October 4 following two weeks of competition between 45 countries and territories across 43 sports. Despite the official slogan “imagine one Asia”, fragmented regional politics came to the fore as the event unfolded.

Just days before the games officially began, tensions between Japan and South Korea flared after an actor portraying a medieval Japanese warlord featured at a welcoming ceremony for the athletes in the host city of Nagoya. The warlord, Toyotomi Hideyoshi, is a local hero in Nagoya but also led the 16th-century Japanese invasion of Korea.

At the 2020 Tokyo Summer Olympics, the South Korean delegation was asked to remove a banner at the athletes’ village containing words attributed to a Korean admiral, Yi Sun-sin, who defeated the Japanese Navy in the same medieval war. With this in mind, the Nagoya ceremony particularly upset South Korea, which filed a complaint with the event organiser.

Historical issues are an area of particular sensitivity between South Korea and Japan. The 16th-century invasion was followed by a Japanese occupation of the Korean peninsula from 1910 to 1945.

title: Op-ed | The UK’S Long and Winding Road Back to Brussels
content: Andy Burnham’s recent party conference speech marked a fundamental shift in the UK’s position on a future relationship with the European Union, effectively abandoning the post-Brexit ‘red lines’ set out in Labour’s 2024 election manifesto. The four options mentioned by the Prime Minister are preserving the status quo, joining a customs union, joining the single market, or full EU membership (‘going all the way’). The 2024 manifesto had explicitly ruled out returning to the customs union or the single market or allowing freedom of movement. Beyond acknowledging that Brexit has done ‘more harm than good’, Burnham has so far given no indication of his preferred option.

title: Miksi kodin netti tuntuu hitaalta, vaikka nopeuden pitäisi olla kunnossa?
content:
Jos kotiin tulee nopea valokuitu ja netti silti takkuilee, syy löytyy usein seinien sisäpuolelta. Suurin osa koetusta pätkimisestä johtuu kodin langattomasta WiFi-verkosta, ei itse nettiyhteydestä. WiFi-signaali heikkenee nopeasti seinien läpi mentäessä ja saattaa ottaa häiriötä naapureiden verkoista tai kodin muista sähkölaitteista.

Jos netti tuntuu hitaalta, käy läpi tämä lista:

Kodin laitteet ja langaton verkko:

  • Sijoita reititin oikein: Älä piilota WiFi-reititintä sähkökaappiin, sohvan taakse tai paksun betoniseinän viereen. Sijoita se keskeiselle paikalle, mielellään hieman lattiatasoa korkeammalle.
  • Käytä kaapelia: Esimerkiksi videopuheluita vaativiin etätöihin käytettävä tietokone tai älytelevisio kannattaa liittää reitittimeen suoraan verkkokaapelilla. Se on varmin tapa estää pätkiminen.
  • Tarkista laitteiston ikä: Vanha reititin ei välttämättä jaksa käsitellä nykyaikaisia nopeuksia. Varmista, että laitteesi on ajan tasalla.
  • Harkitse Mesh-verkkoa: Jos asuntosi on suuri tai monikerroksinen, laadukas Mesh-järjestelmä on paras ratkaisu. Se luo kotiin yhden laajan langattoman verkon, joka kantaa jokaiseen huoneeseen.

title: Former UN food agency official claims he was fired for highlighting hunger in Gaza
content:
Benjamin Davis appealing against dismissal from FAO, after being accused by director general of playing ‘political games’

A former senior UN food agency official has alleged he was fired last week for his work highlighting hunger in Gaza, and has launched an appeal against his dismissal.

Benjamin Davis said the leadership of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) had refused to renew his contract as director of its rural transformation and gender equality division because his team had published a brief on hunger in Gaza and held a seminar on the subject last year, and because he had taken part in weekly “moment of silence” vigils on FAO grounds for those killed.

title: Venezuela: Renewal of UN scrutiny supports victim’s rights in the face of persisting impunity
content:
In response to the UN Human Rights Council’s vote today adopting the resolution that renews the mandate of the Fact-Finding Mission on Venezuela, as well as of the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, for another two years, Amnesty International’s Americas director, Ana Piquer, said: 

“We welcome this decision to continue the scrutiny over the ongoing human rights crisis in Venezuela. Extending the Mission’s crucial work for the next two years reinforces the international community’s interest in justice and accountability for gross human rights violations in the country, including crimes against humanity. This is a clear sign of recognition that the government’s repressive apparatus is still in place while opacity and impunity remain the norm.”

title: Key European Airports Need Permanent Drone Defenses
content:
Drone technology spurred by the war in Ukraine is evolving at a sometimes stupefying pace. From conducting deep strikes to disrupting logistics and evacuating wounded soldiers, unmanned systems are at the heart of modern warfare.

Most important are Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) and counter-UAS, where the European Union and NATO are still a long way behind. Both should recognize the threat to continental security and the most important aspects of civil life, like airports. Counter-drone equipment and personnel should now be deployed at key points like airports, before being replicated more widely.

While Ukraine’s innovative use of drones is providing important lessons, Western countries are not adapting, offering Russia the upper hand in any future conflict. Moscow is already preparing the ground with unregistered drone flights near airports and ports across the continent, and Europe has no clear strategy in response.

Ukraine’s Operation Spider’s Web, in June 2025, used cheap drones launched from trucks parked near Russian military facilities to damage or perhaps destroy 20 or more strategic aircraft, reducing Moscow’s strike and surveillance capabilities.

title: Ebola Death Toll in DRC Tops 4,000; Trump USAID Cuts Fuel Outbreak
content:
We go to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the site of the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. Health authorities believe the outbreak first began in January but was not detected until May, in part due to cuts in global health investments, like the dismantling of USAID. Since then, over 8,000 cases have been recorded, with more than 4,000 fatalities so far. From Bunia, Ituri province, the epicenter of the outbreak, we speak to Congolese journalist Akilimali Chomachoma. Chomachoma describes the strain on the underfunded Congolese healthcare system as the disease spreads. Many frontline workers have not been paid for months.

“We are seeing this outbreak emerge, and really unfurl, in a setting of decreased global health support,” says Craig Spencer, a doctor and public health expert based in the United States who contracted Ebola while on a medical mission to Guinea in 2014. “The U.S. has not shown up in the same way that it has in previous Ebola outbreaks.” Spencer also comments on the “unprecedented” measles outbreak in the United States, which he warns is likely to continue and lead to additional deaths.

title: Ennuste ei ole vaikutusarvio
content:
Keskustelu datakeskushankkeista on käynyt kuumana sen jälkeen, kun Google ilmoitti rakentavansa neljä datakeskusta Suomeen. Yleisemmin kysymys on siitä, miten suurten yksittäisten hankkeiden tai tapahtumien pitäisi näkyä koko talouden ennusteessa. Keskustelusta on unohtunut se, että ennuste ei ole yksittäisten tapahtumien yhteenlaskemista vaan talouden eri ilmiöiden yhteensovittamista, kirjoittaa Etla-kolumnissaan pääekonomisti Jenni Pääkkönen.

Hakukoneyhtiö Google ei ole avannut datakeskushankkeen vaikutusarviota kovinkaan läpinäkyvästi, vaikka monia oletuksia tai tuloksia siitä onkin kerrottu julkisuuteen. Se ei vielä tee arviosta automaattisesti kelvotonta, vaan kertoo siitä, että hanke sisältää monia yrityssalaisuuksia, joita ei voi julkisesti avata.  

Toisaalta yhtiöllä on varmasti myös intressi nostaa esiin hankkeen positiivisia vaikutuksia, sillä suhtautuminen datakeskushankkeisiin on erityisesti Yhdysvalloissa muuttunut sangen nihkeäksi. Siksi annettuihin tietoihin tulee suhtautua tietyllä varauksella.  

Kaiken huminan keskellä on kuitenkin muistettava, että Google on pörssiyhtiö, eikä siten voi julkisesti satuilla ihan mitä tahansa.

title: Mandate of the UN Special Rapporteur on Russia Extended for Another Year
content:
The UN Human Rights Council on October 6 extended the mandate of the Special Rapporteur on the human rights situation in Russia for another year. Russia withdrew its amendment that attempted to delete renewal of the mandate.

The extension is welcome news. The Russia mandate provides an essential independent voice to document the Russian government’s grave human rights violations and serves as a lifeline for the country’s besieged civil society.

The mandate was established in 2022 when, along with its war against Ukraine, the Kremlin launched a draconian crackdown on human rights defenders, independent journalists, political opponents, and other Russian based critics of the war.

title: Montenegro Moves to Seize Vast Real Estate Empire of Fugitive Crime Boss
content:
Authorities in Montenegro might not be able to catch the country's most notorious fugitive crime boss, but they are moving to dismantle his financial empire.

The Special State Prosecutor's Office asked Tuesday the High Court in Podgorica to permanently confiscate a sprawling portfolio of real estate and luxury vehicles it believes is in his or his wife’s possession. While the official statement only identified the targets by their initials, R.Z. and his wife, T.Z., the request appears to be detailing the hidden wealth of the reputed Kavač clan leader Radoje Zvicer and his wife Tamara Zvicer. Local media reports also name the two as the targets of this request.

The timing of this massive forfeiture request is no coincidence. It serves as one of the first major tests of Montenegro's sweeping new "Anti-Mafia Law," passed on September 4. The government hailed the legislation as a "historic step" that has already caused an "earthquake in criminal circles," specifically because it empowers the state to permanently confiscate assets in organized crime cases even before a final judicial verdict is reached.

title: In 1704, Isaac Newton Predicted That the World Will End in 2060
content:
We have become quite used to pronouncements of doom, from scientists predicting the sixth mass extinction due to the measurable effects of climate change, and from religionists declaring the apocalypse due to a surfeit of sin. It’s almost impossible to imagine these two groups of people agreeing on anything other than the ominous portent of their respective messages. But in the early days of the scientific revolution—the days of Shakespeare’s contemporary Francis Bacon, and later 17th century Descartes—it was not at all unusual to find both kinds of reasoning, or unreasoning, in the same person, along with beliefs in magic, divination, astrology, etc.

Yet even in this maelstrom of heterodox thought and practices, Sir Isaac Newton stood out as a particularly odd co-existence of esoteric biblical prophecy, occult beliefs, and a rigid, formal mathematics that not only adhered to the inductive scientific method, but also expanded its potential by applying general axioms to specific cases.

title: More Than 500 U.S. Citizens Have Been Detained, Including Handcuffed or Held at Gunpoint, in Trump’s Immigration Crackdown
content:
Experts have long warned that immigration dragnets and the erosion of civil rights for immigrants will inevitably result in the erosion of rights for citizens.

Since the start of this Trump administration, we’ve watched those warnings come true.

The Trump administration says none of this is happening.

“DHS is NOT arresting U.S. citizens by mistake.” “There are no ‘indiscriminate’ stops.” Allegations of “racial profiling are disgusting, reckless and categorically FALSE.” “The pattern is NOT of law enforcement using force.” “ICE does not zip tie or restrain children.”

But that is precisely what is happening, and at a far larger scale than previously reported.

We know because we have once again done what the government hasn’t:

We have tallied and cataloged every case we can find of an immigration agent holding a citizen during the current administration.

More than 500 cases. That includes:

  • More than a hundred Americans held after agents questioned their citizenship. Nearly all were people of color.
  • At least 70 American children and teens detained, some of whom were handcuffed.
snippet: Experts have long warned that immigration dragnets and the erosion of civil rights for immigrants will inevitably result in the erosion of rights for citizens.

title: Seuran jäsen, hae mukaan työryhmien toimintaan!
content:
Työryhmätoiminta on Kirjastoseuran suola!

Etsimme nyt työryhmiin uusia jäseniä kaudelle 2027–28. Suomen kirjastoseurassa toimii vuonna 2026 kuusi työryhmää. Työryhmiin voit tutustua täällä. Lisätietoja työryhmien toiminnasta saat kunkin ryhmän puheenjohtajalta.

Työryhmiin etsitään jälleen uusia jäseniä. Samalla lomakkeella haetaan sekä työryhmän varsinaiseksi että opiskelijajäseneksi. Huomaathan, että koulutus-ja tutkimustyöryhmän suuren koon vuoksi ryhmään ei valita tällä hakukierroksella täysin uusia edustajia.

Työryhmätoiminta tarjoaa seuran jäsenille mahdollisuuksia verkostoitua, oppia ja kehittää asiantuntijuuttaan. Se tarjoaa vaikuttamiskanavan (suomalaiseen) kirjastotyöhön, auttaa tutustumaan kirjastokenttään valtakunnallisesti ja ryhmässä toimimisesta saa työtodistuksen. Käytännön toimintaan ryhmät saavat apua ja tukea myös seuran toimistolta.

Työryhmän tehtäviä ovat:

  • toimia Kirjastoseuran hallituksen tukena antaen asiantuntija-apua
  • edistää yhdenvertaisuutta ja moninaisuutta kirjastoalalla
  • tukea ammattitaitoa järjestämällä koulutuspäiviä ja ammattitapaamisia sekä tarjoamalla mahdollisuuksia vertaistukeen

title: The EU shelved AI liability rules. Sam Altman has revived the debate.
content:
BRUSSELS — EU parliamentarians are digging in on calls to revive an artificial intelligence liability law after receiving support from an unexpected ally: OpenAI’s Sam Altman.

“If something goes wrong with our models during training, there’s gonna be some version of that we need to be responsible for,” Altman said in an exclusive interview with Decoded by POLITICO released Monday. “There’s gonna need to be a liability framework for companies.”

This spotlight on liability has given influential members of the European Parliament a told-you-so moment after the EU last year scrapped plans to legislate on responsibility and compensation for harms caused by AI makers and agents.

The proposal by the European Commission for an AI liability law was killed amid a deep effort in Brussels to deregulate and reduce the legislative burden on companies — with the Commission arguing at the time that the proposal had little chance of securing sufficient political support.

German conservative lawmaker Axel Voss, who led on the proposal for the European Parliament, wants Brussels to put liability back on the agenda in light of Altman’s comments.

title: Artificial review – Luca Guadagnino takes on OpenAI in muddled tech satire
content:
New York film festival: The origin story of Sam Altman’s company is reimagined as a campy comedy starring Andrew Garfield

On the day that Luca Guadagnino’s film about Sam Altman and OpenAI premiered, Vanity Fair released a cover story on Altman. Alongside glossy portraits from Annie Leibovitz, the world’s pre-eminent portrait photographer, the story describes him as the Oppenheimer of his day, evoking the image of a man leading humanity towards its own inevitable demise at the hands of sentient robots. Altman doesn’t seem to be grappling with much existential angst about the whole thing though: in an interview also released this week, he said that we should be prepared to accept “bad things” in return for the benefits of AI.

How much worse can things get? AI agents have already gone rogue, hacking into government systems and “bruteforcing” UN databases. Last year, a young woman used ChatGPT as a therapist before she killed herself (the software helped her write her suicide note). Studies show that using AI is probably leading us all towards something called cognitive surrender, which does not seem like the best use of your one wild and precious life.

title: What Europe’s EU Inc. framework for boosting competitiveness can and should learn from startup fraud in the US
content:
The European Parliament and the Council of the European Union are currently debating EU Inc, draft legislation seeking to establish a single set of rules for starting, operating, and growing a business across EU member states. The proposed framework is designed to make business registration and operation within the EU faster, easier, and more harmonised.

The proposed “28th regime” promises company registration within 48 hours for under €100 via fully digitalised procedures – including for raising capital and accessing the stock market, and simplified liquidation proceedings to make dissolving and relaunching a business more seamless. The proposal is part of the broader EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy, whose ambition is to narrow the innovation gap between the EU and its global competitors, notably the United States.

title: Sudan’s death toll in 2025 could be as high as 100,000: how we did the count
content:
Estimates of the number of people directly killed in Sudan’s civil war vary widely, in part because counting casualties in active conflict zones is extremely difficult. In 2025, for instance, one conflict monitoring organisation reported around 19,000 direct deaths from political violence across Sudan. Other research teams put the toll at more than 70,000.

Conflict researcher Paola Vesco and her team have developed a model that helps measure the uncertainty around such conflict death estimates. Their approach takes into account the tendency of conflict datasets to underestimate fatalities, and provides a more realistic range of possible death tolls. They explain how their model could improve estimates in conflicts like Sudan’s.

The number of people killed in Sudan’s war since it began in April 2023 remains contested. Deaths in 2025 have been especially hard to establish as communications were cut and humanitarian access was blocked.

In 2025, fighting intensified as the Rapid Support Forces – a paramilitary group which has fought the Sudanese army for control of the state since 2023 – advanced in Darfur and North Kordofan. Civilian deaths and displacement rose.

title: Asumisen tarpeet moninaistuvat – Asuntotuotannon on uudistuttava
content:
Rakennustietosäätiön uusi tietosynteesi kokoaa tutkimustiedon ja alan asiantuntijoiden näkemykset siitä, miten suomalaisen asuntotuotannon tulisi vastata väestön, kotitalouksien ja elämäntapojen muutoksiin.

Väestö ikääntyy, yksinasuminen yleistyy ja maahanmuutto lisää asumistarpeiden kirjoa ja työn sekä arjen tavat muuttuvat. Etä- ja hybridityö tekevät kodista yhä useammin myös työtilan. Monipaikkaisuus hajauttaa arkea useaan paikkaan ja eri elämänvaiheet kasvattavat tarvetta asunnoille, jotka mukautuvat erilaisiin käyttötapoihin. Myös kotitalouksien maksukyky asettaa asumiselle reunaehtoja.

Asuntokanta muuttuu huomattavasti hitaammin kuin väestö ja elämäntavat, joten tämän päivän asuntotuotannon ratkaisut määrittävät asumisen mahdollisuuksia vuosikymmeniksi. Jos tuotetut asunnot ja asuinympäristöt eivät vastaa kotitalouksien arjen ja tilan tarpeita tai taloudellisiin mahdollisuuksiin, seurauksena voi olla heikko kysyntä, vajaakäyttö, kalliit muutostyöt tai rakennusten elinkaaren ennenaikainen päättyminen.

The University of Helsinki has generated more than 30 research-based spinouts with a combined value in excess of €400 million.

At Nokia Research Center, he led teams that advanced research findings and technology towards commercial products. As a startup entrepreneur, CEO, advisor and board member he has subsequently built business operations that bridge technology, market demand and societal needs.

title: Vallankumouksellista kehitystä Steve Jobsin malliin
content:
Tuulikki Närhinsalo

”Nosta katseesi. Katso ympärillesi. Ole läsnä”. Tällainen teksti ilmestyi parisen vuotta sitten Kansallisoopperan tekstityslaitteeseen luettavaksi ennen esityksen alkua. Sillä haluttaneen viestittää, että nyt on aika lakata tuijottamasta kännykän ruutua ja rauhoittua kokemaan se yhteisöllisyyden tunne, jonka oopperan tai baletin seuraaminen tarjoaa. Lähes hätkähdin, kun Mason Batesin oopperan The (R)evolution of Steve Jobs viimeinen repliikki ja sen kaikkein tärkein sanoma, jonka Jobsin vaimo laulaa miehensä kauniisti rakennetussa muistotilaisuudessa, on tekstilaitteeseen suomennettuna ”Nostakaa katseenne, katsokaa pois laitteistanne”. Miten tärkeä viesti meille kaikille!

Mahdollisimman nopealle teknologian kehittämiselle elämänsä pyhittänyt Steve Jobs, jonka epäterveellisen hektinen ja itsekeskeinen elämäntapa tuhosi naissuhteita, työyhteisöjä ja lopulta hänen terveytensä, haki ja sai helpotusta elämänsä kiemuroihin buddhalaisuudesta. Tämä teema on oopperassa vahvasti mukana. Elontaipaleensa loppumetreillä Jobs pohtii tekemiään valintoja ja niiden seurauksia kriittisesti munkkiystävänsä kanssa.

title: “What we are standing for is a right to say no”
content:
For more than a decade, Antonia Burke travelled across Australia listening to First Nations people describe the impacts of government decisions on their lives. Over the years, she heard stories of oppression, injustice and intergenerational trauma. As a First Nations woman from the Yanyuwa and Garrwa people from the Northern Territory, Antonia understands first-hand how government policies can shape lives. That understanding took on new urgency when she saw the extent of offshore oil and gas development across the Arafura and Timor Seas, waters that sustain communities, cultures and marine life across Australia, Timor-Leste, Papua New Guinea and Indonesia. First Nations people in Australia call these waters “Sea Country” –  a source of identity that holds stories and songlines that have guided people for generations.

As Founder and Director of Sea of Nations, Antonia works with First Nations people and coastal communities to hold decision makers accountable for ensuring meaningful consultation and consent before decisions affecting their territories are made. Here, she shares her experience:

title: Lawmakers Introduce Multiple Laws to Curb Flock After 404 Media Coverage
content:
Multiple Democrat, Republican, and Independent lawmakers have introduced new pieces of legislation that, if passed, would dramatically curb federal agencies’ access to Flock cameras, with the lawmakers referencing reporting by 404 Media in their explanations for why the legislation is needed.

On Friday Senator Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), and Senator Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) announced the Ban Flock Act, which would prohibit federal agencies from using automatic license plate readers (ALPRs) and block federal funding from state and local governments that use the cameras. It would also let Americans sue the federal government for violation of their rights through ALPRs.

title: French High School Students Lead Mass Protests over School Funding, Inequality; Thousands Arrested
content:
Nearly 2,000 French high schools are blockaded or closed today amid massive student-led protests over school funding and inequality. The demonstrations began in September at a single school in the economically deprived suburbs of Paris, where students protested teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and dilapidated school buildings beset by rats, falling debris and more. But the scope of the protests has widened amid a violent crackdown by French police. French authorities have arrested more than 5,000 people, largely underage students, since the movement began. Violent police tactics have led to serious injuries. One protester lost an eye after being hit by a rubber bullet, while another lost a hand when he picked up a police stun grenade.

We hear from an anonymous protester who describes the violence meted out on students, who “aren’t even adults yet,” and from Claire Vigneau, general secretary of Fédération Syndicale Étudiante, the French student union, who reports from a protest in Rennes, Brittany, “where we are trying to escape from the policemen that are chasing us with tear gas and with water cannon[s].”

title: Missing Lao Critic in Thailand Feared ‘Disappeared’
content:
Three weeks ago, 26-year-old Lao activist Khieo Lapchanh, an asylum seeker in Thailand, vanished in Samut Sakhon province following his shift at the restaurant where he worked.

Khieo’s disappearance in the early hours of September 15 came one day before his first interview with the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) in Bangkok. Thai authorities have yet to provide any information regarding his whereabouts.

Khieo had been posting videos critical of the Lao government to his Facebook page, Khiew Channel, which had about 158,000 followers. According to Manushya Foundation, a rights group that supported him, he had faced coordinated harassment, doxxing, and death threats. After Lao officials visited his mother's home in Laos this year on March 31 and April 17 concerning his activities, Khieo stopped posting political content.

Given the threats he faced and the history of enforced disappearances of Lao activists both in Laos and abroad, Thai authorities should urgently locate him.

title: Our Reporter Spent 10 Weeks Gambling on DraftKings. Here Are 5 Things He Learned.
content:
Online gambling has surged in the U.S. since the Supreme Court allowed states to legalize sports betting in 2018, prompting public health concerns about gambling addiction and calls for stricter consumer protections. Online sportsbooks such as DraftKings and FanDuel have touted “responsible gaming” features as evidence that they are taking appropriate steps to protect consumers from spiraling out of control.

Reporter Jake Pearson put these safeguards to the test. Bankrolled by ProPublica, he mimicked the betting patterns of a problem gambler for 10 weeks, consulting a panel of addiction specialists, recovering gambling addicts and professional sports bettors for advice.

He found that the safety features were overpowered by the app’s product design and promotions that pushed him to continue gambling.

Pearson detailed his entire journey, which you can read here. Here are five takeaways from his investigation.

title: German search engine ditches Mistral, bets on Chinese open-source AI
content:
BERLIN — A Berlin-based search engine used by government services is dropping its French AI partner, Mistral, in favor of open-source models, including those from China, its CEO told POLITICO.

“We are disappointed with the quality of Mistral,” Ecosia founder and CEO Christian Kroll said in an interview, stating that the models from France’s flagship AI lab are now “a year behind” the competition.

Ecosia — a German web browser and search engine that has built its brand on support for climate action and independence from non-European tech — is used by institutions ranging from Germany’s federal environment ministry to the U.K.’s National Health Service.

In May, it replaced the American giant OpenAI with Mistral as its AI provider. But the company experienced recurring technical problems, including overloaded servers, Kroll said. “We were simply too large a customer for Mistral,” Kroll said

title: Who owns ‘brain rot’? Inside the international legal drama over a beloved meme
content:
Copyright law in the US only applies to human-made creations, but AI characters like Tung Tung Tung Sahur are challenging that

One of the most beloved characters in an absurdist genre of online video content has become the center of an international legal battle that could determine where human creativity ends and artificial intelligence begins.

Tung Tung Tung Sahur, also known as Triple T, was created in 2025 by an Indonesian teen who goes by the username Noxa, using OpenAI’s image-generation tool. Based on a kentongan – a type of drum used to wake south-east Asian Muslims for their pre-dawn meal during Ramadan – the character is an anthropomorphized version of the instrument with a broad smile and a vacant stare. He sits under the umbrella of “Italian brain rot” internet videos.

title: A camera combined with AI could help further diagnosis of movement disorders like spinal muscular atrophy in newborns
content:
Detecting impaired motor function as early as possible after birth with the help of a standard camera linked to intelligent systems can help in diagnosing infantile conditions characterised by hypotonia: reduction or loss of active muscle movement. A research team is investigating this approach based on the work carried out on babies with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), a rare genetic neuromuscular disorder.

In 2019, the drug Zolgensma made headline news as the world’s most expensive treatment. The price of this medicine for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) has been set at nearly 2 million euros per injection.

And, at the same time, what an extraordinary breakthrough! It promises to provide a definitive cure for a genetic disease that, if survivors do live, leads to extremely severe disabilities in children affected by what is the world’s first hereditary peripheral neurological disorder.

Behind these staggering figures lies an urgent medical situation. For these therapies to be effective, it is essential to identify the condition as early as possible. This is precisely the challenge our team set out to tackle, by using an ordinary camera coupled with artificial intelligence.

title: Why old dogs might be able to teach Alzheimer’s researchers new tricks
content:
Most people know someone with Alzheimer’s disease. When I was growing up, my grandmother struggled with dementia, and I saw firsthand how difficult that was for our family.

That experience was one reason I became a neurotoxicologist who studies how misshapen proteins and inflammation in the brain can increase over time and cause dementia. While there are ways to treat the symptoms of dementia, researchers are still in search of a cure.

Alzheimer’s disease and other types of dementia are difficult to study, in part because diagnosing the disease early in people is challenging. These diseases typically begin developing two decades prior to most symptoms that would prompt someone to see a clinician. As a result, most researchers use mouse models to test potential therapies for Alzheimer’s.

title: Edellä-foorumi sai kiitosta keskusteluista – järjestäjä pohtii tapahtumalle jatkoa
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Edellä – Vihreän aatteen foorumi järjestettiin Helsingissä 18.–19. syyskuuta. Tapahtuman jälkeen tunnelmat ovat järjestäjä Sivistysliitto Vision pääsihteerin Katja Alvoitun mukaan erittäin myönteiset.

"Päällimmäinen ja tärkein fiilis on se, että konsepti kantoi. Periaatteellisella tasolla liikkuvat keskustelut tutkijoiden, poliitikkojen, tietokirjailijoiden ja aktivistien kanssa olivat ihan valtavan inspiroivia", Alvoittu sanoo.

Hänen mukaansa juuri tämänkaltaisen ajatustenvaihdon luonteva paikka on sivistysliiton tapahtumassa.

content:
(Beirut) – The Houthi de facto authorities in Yemen have sent at least eight people involved in human rights and humanitarian work for criminal prosecution, on espionage-related charges punishable by death, since August 18, 2026, Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch said today. They include two United Nations employees, a UN consultant, and five people who worked with international and local civil society organizations on a range of issues, including health, human rights, and humanitarian aid. 

The Houthis should immediately halt these prosecutions and unconditionally release the eight people whose cases were sent to the prosecution, as well as the scores of other UN staff and civil society workers the Houthis have arbitrarily detained over the past two years.

title: Jailed Albanian mayor uses AI avatar to make deepfake speech
content:
TIRANA, Albania — Tirana Mayor Erion Veliaj has caused a stir with a video pledge of free school lunches for all the capital’s children. There’s one problem: Veliaj is currently in prison, and the blue-suited figure making the heartfelt announcement is AI-generated.

In an Instagram post on his official profile labeled as AI-generated, the video likeness of the 46-year-old appears in front of the Albanian and municipal flags, listing his achievements in office while reiterating his promise of free school lunches for the city’s kids. 

“I made another commitment that I will never forget: food in schools,” says the Veliaj clone. “I will keep this promise even from this cell where they have locked me up.”

Veliaj has been in prison in the coastal city of Durres since early 2025 amid investigations over allegations of corruption and financial crimes. He denies any wrongdoing. 

“My hostage situation has been going on for 20 months, and I can only greet you with artificial intelligence,” his avatar says. “I will continue to work even from the cell … I hug you with longing, you and your wonderful children.”

title: Nobel physics prize awarded for discovery of ‘ghostly messengers’ from the cosmos
content:
The 2026 Nobel prize for physics has been awarded to US-based researcher Francis Halzen for his discovery of high energy neutrino particles from space.

The Nobel committee said Halzen has made “decisive contributions” to the discovery of “neutrinos of astrophysical origin” with IceCube, an experiment installed under ice at the South Pole.

Ellen Moons, secretary general of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, described these neutrinos as “ghostly messengers”. This references the fact the particles have nearly no mass and pass through solid objects with hardly any interaction. In fact, billions of neutrinos pass through any given person on Earth every second.

Most of these neutrinos are emitted by the Sun. However, high energy neutrinos coming from elsewhere in the cosmos also reach our planet. These neutrinos are about a billion times rarer than those that stream out from the Sun.

They originate from diverse sources, such as black holes located at the hearts of distant galaxies that accelerate particles to extreme energies.

title: Taylor Swift’s new video marks her ghostly return to Daphne du Maurier’s Rebecca
content:
In 2020, Taylor Swift told us she read Daphne du Maurier’s Rebecca, the 1938 bestseller about a young bride haunted by the memory of her husband’s glamorous first wife. Swift described how it inspired her while she was writing Tolerate It for her ninth studio album Evermore, which came out the same year.

The song was about trying hard to impress an older partner and going unappreciated. Swift explained that she’d identified with the book’s narrator, known only as Mrs de Winter (the successor of Maxim de Winter’s late first wife, Rebecca): “She’s trying so hard […] to impress him and he’s just tolerating her.”

Six years later, Swift returns to Manderley – the fictional Cornwall estate in which Rebecca is set – with her new single Patient Zero and its self-directed music video, which was unveiled at the VMAs (the MTV Video Music Awards). It’s the latest entry in the genre of Swift gothic, a strand of her music that takes on doubles, hauntings and darkness. Gothic doubles pop up in the music videos for Anti-Hero and Out of the Woods, for instance.

title: EVA: S2-opetuksesta luovuttava – maahanmuuttajaoppilaiden kielituki yhteisiin luokkiin
content:
Maahanmuuttajataustaisten oppilaiden erillisopetusta pitää vähentää tuntuvasti ja suomen kielen oppimista siirtää yhteisiin luokkiin, esitetään Elinkeinoelämän valtuuskunta EVAn analyysissä. Ehdotuksessa luovutaan S2-opetuksesta ja muiden kuin kotimaisten kielten oman äidinkielen opetuksesta.

Taustalla on tieto kansainvälisesti poikkeuksellisen suurista eroista maahanmuuttajataustaisten ja kantaväestön oppimiseroissa Suomessa. PISA-tuloksissa juopa säilyy suurena, vaikka oppilaiden sosioekonominen asema ja kotikieli huomioidaan. Aiheesta kirjoitti hiljattain myös Verden kolumnisti Eva Tawasoli.

EVAn mukaan ongelma ei poistu myöskään Suomessa syntyneiden toisen polven maahanmuuttajien kohdalla.

Analyysin laatineen ekonomisti Sanna Kurrosen mukaan yksi mahdollinen syy on se, että maahanmuuttajataustaiset oppilaat laajalti eriytetään muista oppilaista. Suomessa oppilas voi opiskella erillisissä ryhmissä valmistavassa opetuksessa, suomi toisena kielenä eli S2-opetuksessa, oman äidinkielen opetuksessa sekä oman uskonnon opetuksessa.

title: Tunisia: Power, Water Shortages Endanger Rights
content:
(Beirut) – Tunisian authorities failed to ensure an adequate supply of electricity and water during two months of extreme summer heat, undermining the right to health and endangering lives, Human Rights Watch said today. President Kais Saied blamed the shortages on sabotage, yet authorities failed to provide transparent information and instead cracked down on protesters. 

Rolling power outages left hospitals and water pumping stations without electricity and households without running water, interrupted critical medical procedures, and contributed to a nationwide shortage of drinking water. Doctors and human rights groups have reported a rise in heat-related hospitalizations and deaths exacerbated by the cuts, including among detainees.

title: OpenAI’s Jason Kwon gave even-toned, reassuring answers to the Australian government. Did … ChatGPT write this?
content:
Kwon’s answers were provided in a helpful, quiet and calm manner, but his mea culpa left the audience not much the wiser

Open AI’s Jason Kwon flew 15 hours from San Francisco to Sydney to give the company’s first in-person mea culpa after it admitted – in an unsigned email, to a public departmental inbox – that one of its AI agents had accessed a Services Australia website without authorisation and grabbed data related to Medicare.

Kwon – polite, friendly, even-toned – got through a potentially dicey parliamentary committee hearing unscathed, promising to do better and pledging assistance to Australia. No missteps, no viral moments, just delivering his answers helpfully, in a quiet and calm manner, sympathising with the questioner and the point they were making.

title: October 7: a Palestinian-Israeli memoir seeks to break the cycle of violence
content:
Since the Hamas attacks of October 7, 2023, the world has witnessed unimaginable, almost constant violence in Gaza and the West Bank. But people’s understanding of these events is not universal – each person is exposed to a particular set of narratives surrounding history, victimhood and trauma.

The vast majority of news reports, social media posts, videos, and books that have covered the events since October 7, 2023 can be defined as what I call “conflict media”, which reproduces the divisions of the conflict it describes, perpetuating it to the point where the media itself becomes a weapon in an information war.

As a scholar of the Middle East, I have rarely – though not never – encountered conflict media’s opposite, which I call “resolution media”.

The most famous works of resolution media have emerged after a conflict ends, and highlight the universal suffering of war. Wilfred Owen’s first world war poem Dulce et Decorum Est, for instance, is still widely quoted to expose “the old Lie” that it is “sweet and fitting” to die for one’s country.

title: The death of a Russian plague researcher, explained by a microbiologist
content:
Conflicting information about the death of a lab worker at a Russian plague research institute has fuelled fears about the possibility of pneumonic plague spreading.

Nearly 200 people are in quarantine in Siberia after 28-year-old Darya Shipilova fell ill at work and later died on October 2.

The exact circumstances of her death are unknown. A senior Russian official posted on social media last week that Shipilova “had died from the plague” – before editing the post to add “possibly”. Russia’s health watchdog has since stated she died from “pneumonia of unknown etiology”.

Local media reports suggested she was infected following an accident at the lab where she worked, the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East. But these have not been confirmed.

So, what is plague, and how does it spread? Should we be worried?

Plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. The bacteria generally live in ground-dwelling rodents such as rats and prairie dogs, but can also infect humans.

The same Y. pestis bacteria can cause three different types of plague.

title: Transatlantic Biotech Spurs Cancer Breakthroughs
content:
The advances are astounding. A personalized cancer vaccine developed with messenger RNA (mRNA) technology extends the survival of melanoma patients. It trains patients’ immune systems to recognize and attack unique mutated proteins found only on their tumor cells. Another new mRNA drug, Daraxonrasib, doubles the life expectancy of pancreatic cancer patients.

These breakthroughs result from longstanding cooperation between US and European researchers and firms.

Start with the basic research. In 2005, Hungarian Katalin Karikó and American Drew Weissman at the University of Pennsylvania showed that modifying the nucleoside building blocks of synthetic mRNA could reduce unwanted inflammatory responses while improving protein production. Their work helped make therapeutic mRNA viable and later earned them the 2023 Nobel Prize.

The technology then moved across the Atlantic.

Germany’s BioNTech pursued mRNA and individualized cancer immunotherapies long before the COVID-19 pandemic. When the pandemic arrived, BioNTech partnered with US pharma giant Pfizer to develop and distribute the COVID vaccine.

title: A copyright advent calendar – making copyright literacy a little more playful
content:
Erica Levi is the he copyright lead at Lanchester Library, Coventry University. Her team specialises in embedding Open Educational Resources in teaching at the university.  She advises and train colleagues on copyright and licences. Since copyright still seems like a dreary topic for most colleagues, she set herself a mission to develop online educational games. She tell us….

When Halloween decorations appear in shops before we have quite accepted that summer is over, and Christmas merchandise follows closely behind, my thoughts inevitably turn to how to bring copyright into it. Perhaps that is an occupational hazard?

But there is a serious idea behind it. Over the years, I have become increasingly interested in how we can make copyright education feel less daunting and more inviting. Copyright is important, but that doesn’t mean learning about it always has to involve lengthy guidance, formal training, or lots of text. Sometimes a quiz, a game or a slightly silly seasonal scenario can start a conversation just as effectively.

Certain times of year also give us a ready-made excuse to try something different. I like to latch onto calendar events, really. 

Why make copyright seasonal?

title: What could the EU Artists’ Charter look like? Read the sector blueprint
content:
Imagine your ideal working life in culture. How are you paid? Do you have the space and freedom to create? What support can you count on if you fall ill? What happens to your rights if you work across borders? 

Now try to document this perfect condition and think about who should do what to make it happen. 

That’s what we at Culture Action Europe have been working on over the past five months with our members. Together, we wrote the paper ‘Towards the EU Artists’ Charter: A Sector Blueprint.’ It is our contribution to the forthcoming official document of the European Commission, the EU Artists’ Charter, that we expect mid-2027 and that should outline fundamental principles, guidance, and commitments for fair working conditions in the cultural and creative sectors. 

The Action Group on Working Conditions developed the Charter Blueprint, co-facilitated by Culture Action Europe and Platform ACCT. The process brought together 40 representatives of cultural organisations and European networks from our membership.

title: Hands Off Our Census: Comments due November 2
content:
The US Census, conducted once every 10 years, has an importance that is difficult to overstate. The goal of every census is to “count everyone once, only once, and in the right place". While most people probably associate the Census with apportionment of seats in the House of Representatives, that is not its only purpose.  The data are used for the following decade to make decisions on school funding, disaster preparedness, public health infrastructure, roads and traffic patterns, and nearly every other facet of daily life for American residents. 

There are three monumental changes currently proposed to how the census would operate:

  • Many residents would no longer be counted, including work-visa holders, international students, and other non-citizen residents.
  • People may be counted in the wrong place, using tax records as addresses instead of where folks actually live, who may be in a different location due to moving, college, service members, and others.
  • For the first time since 1790, race and ethnicity questions would be prohibited, which would mean that the US, at state, federal, and local levels, would not have reliable race/ethnicity data.

title: Meet Issa Amro: Palestinian Human Rights Advocate Attacked by Settlers, Detained by Israeli Army
content:
We speak with Palestinian human rights defender Issa Amro after he was detained at an Israeli military base for seven hours on Friday. Amro, the founder of the Hebron-based group Youth Against Settlements, was helping a Palestinian family that he says had been attacked by armed Israeli settlers at their farmhouse outside Hebron in the occupied West Bank. Amro says when Israeli soldiers arrived, they ignored the settlers and instead targeted the Palestinians, including him. Amro tells Democracy Now! that soldiers handcuffed and blindfolded him before transporting him to the base in the back of a military vehicle. He was freed after an international outcry over his arrest.

“What happened to me is happening to many Palestinian families and many Palestinian human rights defenders and many Palestinian journalists,” says Amro. “It’s not the first time. It’s not the last time. We have to keep working to make occupation [and] apartheid costly and make this kind of human rights violation costly for the offenders.”

title: Quantum transition: the current legal and regulatory landscape for businesses
content:
The quantum transition is approaching fast, while the legal and regulatory landscape is only beginning to take shape. For businesses, the question is not whether quantum technologies will reshape opportunities and risks, but how soon and how prepared they will be when it happens. In this alert, our technology lawyers explain why the time to act is now, what practical steps businesses should be taking and why there is no time to wait for the regulatory framework to catch up.

Quantum technology is no longer a distant research concept. The technology is evolving at speed, and we are nearing a “tipping point” where the fruits of research will mature into commercial applications. Organizations that understand the operational and legal implications of quantum transition now will be far better placed and secured than those that wait.

title: As Belarus plans a new unit at Astravyets NPP, experts do not mince their words: A catastrophe is possible

The latest National Threat Assessment, cited by ELTA, notes that Belarus plans to build a third unit at the Astravyets Nuclear Power Plant alongside the two already in operation.

“Belarusian Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Karankevich publicly announced Belarus’s decision to build a third unit at the Astravyets Nuclear Power Plant site in November 2025. He also said that an assessment of the feasibility of building a new nuclear power plant in the Mogilev Region was continuing,” the intelligence services said.

title: Christa Pike’s Suffering Highlights Inhumanity of Death Penalty
content:
Today, Christa Pike remains unconscious on a ventilator, and in critical condition after the Tennessee government’s failed execution attempt.  

Doctors had warned that her medical condition could make the state’s execution method, lethal injection, exceptionally painful and cruel. In fact, it was barbaric. Authorities tried to insert an IV line for an hour on September 30, using at least seven needles in her left arm. One looked bent as they removed it. Two doses of lethal injection drugs left her unconscious, severely injured, but alive. 

This is the second botched execution in Tennessee over the last several months. Neither case is isolated: nationwide, around 7 percent of execution attempts by lethal injection have either resulted in prolonged visible suffering before death or, as in Pike’s case, left people alive, in some instances only barely. There may be far more suffering that we just can’t see: a federal magistrate judge in Ohio found the dose of one commonly used lethal injection drug is not enough to render the person sufficiently unconscious so they don’t feel “needless pain.”

title: Digital Diogenes or If I Stay Here, Something Precious in Me Will Die
content:
It’s been a long time since images stopped being sacred. They are simply one of the millions of scraps in which I melt.

I am everywhere and everything that can be. And yet I am in a place: this sort of cage called identity, built of fake nostalgia and estrangement from myself. And if I stay here, something precious in me will die.

I dissolve into all the fragments of myself I have chosen to accumulate. The photographs I keep on my phone are not decisions, but rather an unconscious extension of my identity. I am what is worth looking at and, above all, what is worth not deleting.

When I take a photo, or save an image because I find it funny, I do so not as an act of significance, but as a mechanical one because that’s the way of existing online.
snippet: It’s been a long time since images stopped being sacred. They are simply one of the millions of scraps in which I melt.

title: Internet Archive to Honor Poynter Institute and Investigative Reporters and Editors with 2026 Hero Award for Preserving Local News Online
content:
The Internet Archive is proud to announce that the Poynter Institute and Investigative Reporters and Editors (IRE) will receive the 2026 Internet Archive Hero Award for their leadership in preserving local news online.

The Internet Archive Hero Award recognizes individuals and organizations that have demonstrated leadership in making information available to people around the world. The Poynter Institute, a 50-year-old nonprofit that works to strengthen journalism and train journalists, and IRE, a member-driven nonprofit that has spent 50 years helping journalists do better investigative work, have made preservation a vital part of their work.

Local journalism is the first draft of history, and often the only record of what happened in a community. But as news increasingly moves online, that record is at risk. Stories can disappear when a newsroom closes, a website changes platforms, or digital archives are neglected. At the same time, major news publishers and media organizations are restricting access to web archiving tools like the Wayback Machine, making it harder to preserve the journalism being published today.

title: OpenAI “rogue” agent activities found on Wikimedia projects
content:
Recently, multiple organisations have disclosed how clusters of so-called “rogue” AI agents attempted to break into websites and online services, sometimes successfully. Agents from OpenAI’s environment, in particular, are known to have used other public wikis (collaboratively edited websites not owned by us) to communicate and coordinate with each other.

These types of successful intrusions can expose sensitive data or disrupt website services that users rely on, while clusters of agents can attempt attacks at a scale that is difficult for defenders to manage. They affect people behind the websites who may not understand the nature of the attack, or have the tools to effectively fight back. For a site like Wikipedia, agents might find and use security vulnerabilities or make misleading edits at scale. Wikipedia’s volunteer editors and the Wikimedia Foundation’s security teams have to detect and undo that activity.

title: Cocaine Boatmen Are Being Blown Up By US Airstrikes, But The Drugs Keep Flowing From Colombia
content:
First, you hear the high-pitched whine of drones overhead. Next comes the boom of explosions.

“And then in the following days, the sea brings in a jerrycan, pieces of a boat, drugs, people too,” says Alberto, a local businessman living on the Colombian peninsula of La Guajira.

This grim sequence of events has become familiar for those based along this arid strip of desert, whose shores are lapped by a part of the Caribbean Sea that has been the site of some 20 deadly U.S. strikes on speedboats over the past year.

The U.S. military campaign against the alleged “narco-terrorists” manning these vessels, known as Operation Southern Spear, has faded from headline news since the first attack was launched over a year ago on September 2. 

Yet it continues to destroy small boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific — with at least 235 dead in some 70 strikes so far — in the face of heavy criticism from legal experts and rights groups, who call it an ineffective program of what are essentially extrajudicial murders.

title: 300 Years Before ChatGPT, Jonathan Swift’s Gulliver’s Travels Imagined Machines Writing Books and Producing Knowledge (1726)
content: The printing press was invented in the middle of the fifteenth century, and it’s been downhill for the written word ever since. Even before then, arguments that the volume of writing being done far outstripped the value of that writing surely weren’t unheard of. Whatever the era, the most incisive remarks on the apparent victory of verbal quantity over verbal quality tend to have come from writers themselves. No less a satirist than Jonathan Swift made it one of his many targets in Gulliver’s Travels (1726), imagining an elaborate machine of wood and wire called “the Engine” (see illustration above) that automatically generates text, though few remember it — or rather, few remembered it until the rise of large language models in the real world.

title: Sananvapaus täytyy huomioida turvallisuuspolitiikassa
content:
Sananvapauden suhde kansalliseen turvallisuuteen on monisäikeinen ja haastava. Nopeasti muuttuneessa turvallisuusympäristössä tarvitaan keskustelua sananvapaudesta ja sen turvaamisesta keskeisenä demokraattisena oikeutena.

Sananvapaudessa on kyse jokaisen oikeudesta ilmaista itseään valitsemallaan tavalla, esimerkiksi sosiaalisessa mediassa, poliittisessa mielipideartikkelissa tai vaikka taiteen välityksellä. Sananvapaus on turvattu Suomen perustuslaissa ja kansainvälisissä ihmisoikeussopimuksissa.

Sananvapaus on keskeinen demokraattinen oikeus ja vahva demokratia on olennainen osa kansallista turvallisuuttamme. Valtioneuvoston julkaisema Kansallisen turvallisuuden strategia 2026–35 määrittelee Suomen ydinintresseinä muun muassa demokraattisen valtiojärjestyksen ja oikeusvaltion. Strategian tavoite on yhteiskunnan hyvinvoinnin ja turvallisuuden suojaaminen varmistamalla valtion jatku­vuus, Suomen valtiosuvereniteetin ja alueellisen koskemattomuuden turvaaminen sekä demokraattisen valtiojärjestyksen ja oikeusvaltion suojaaminen, ja yhteiskunnan vakauden vahvistaminen.

title: How ProPublica Reporters Became Private School Owners in 24 Hours
content:
It began as a casual question — and a flicker of curiosity — uttered during a meeting of ProPublica journalists who this year are reporting on publicly funded private schools. We were discussing how, in many states, basically anyone can open a private school wherever they want. No experience, no training, no curriculum required.

One of our editors jumped in and asked: What if ProPublica tried to establish a private school?

We were intrigued. We are longtime education reporters, not educators. Would that matter? Where, if anywhere, do states draw the line on who is fit to run a school — and in some cases, collect public money to fund their ventures? 

We decided that testing the thesis that anyone can open a school would be valuable to our ongoing reporting, particularly at a time when we have found that private schools are growing rapidly across the country — in barns, farms, co-working spaces, people’s homes and parks. These new schools are fueled by taxpayer-funded vouchers and other programs, and our reporting has revealed states have little interest in monitoring them.

title: Indigenous digital activists share one TikTok account to bring their languages into digital spaces
content:
@ActLenguas showcases the linguistic diversity found across Latin America. A different language every week.

Originally published on Rising Voices

Online content in English represents more than half of the written content available on the internet, despite the fact that around 16% of the world's population speaks this language. This inequality is also reflected in the presence of Indigenous and minoritized languages in digital spaces. 

Faced with this scenario, Global Voices and Rising Voices have been promoting initiatives that seek to democratize digital spaces, strengthen linguistic diversity, and contribute to Indigenous and minoritized languages, while also creating networks and connections among communities of speakers. Through campaigns, translation communities, gatherings, and other spaces for peer learning and exchange, these initiatives seek to share technologies that respond to communities’ needs and make visible the different ways in which speakers of these languages are already creating, communicating, and transforming them on the Internet.

title: Arkkitehtuurin Finlandia -palkinto Kuusijärven savusaunoille – ”Julkista rakentamista parhaimmillaan”
content:
Suomen Arkkitehtiliitto SAFA myöntää Arkkitehtuurin Finlandia -palkinnon nyt 13. kerran.

Neljän finalistikohteen joukosta voittajan valitsi tämän vuoden tuomari, eurooppalaiseen filosofiaan ja aatehistoriaan erikoistunut tutkija ja tietokirjailija Timo Miettinen.

Voittajaa valitessaan Timo Miettinen pohti, mikä ehdokkaista ilmaisee parhaiten sitä, mitä suomalaisina olemme tai haluamme olla.

”Kuusijärven savusaunat ovat julkista rakentamista parhaimmillaan. Ne osoittavat, että kauneus, kestävyys ja korkea tekninen laatu voivat kuulua kaikille”, Miettinen sanoo.

”Kohteessa yhdistyvät tekninen taidokkuus, esteettinen herkkyys, yhteisöllisyys, luonnon kunnioittaminen ja saavutettavuus. Se tarjoaa meille kaikille paikan sekä hiljentymiseen että yhdessäoloon.”

Miettinen nostaa perusteluissaan esiin erityisesti saunomisrituaalin ja saunojan kulkemisen rakennuksissa ja niiden välillä.

”Pukuhuoneesta siirrytään ulkotilan kautta saunaan ja edelleen veden äärelle. Metsän tuoksut, viileä ilma, savu ja tummat puupinnat liittyvät osaksi harkittua rituaalia. Saunojen niukka valaistus ja suljettu mittakaava luovat suojan, josta avaudutaan takaisin metsään ja järvimaisemaan”, Miettinen arvioi.

title: Är du konstnär eller författare?
content:
Inom det kommande året blir fem av våra Elfvik-ateljéer lediga. Stipendielägenheterna finns på Busholmen i Helsingfors och kan sökas av professionella konstnärer och författare.

För snart tio år sedan flyttade våra första stipendiater in i de sammanlagt 14 då splitternya Elfvik-ateljélägenheterna på Busholmen i Helsingfors.

Snart tar den femåriga stipendieperioden slut för flera hyresgäster och därför frigörs fem lägenheter under det kommande året.

En lägenhet blir tillgänglig i januari, två i maj och två i oktober 2027.

Ateljélägenheterna är främst för svenskspråkiga professionella konstnärer och skådespelare i Finland. Vi beviljar lägenhetsstipendierna för förtjänstfull verksamhet som skapande konstnär.

title: Europe’s AI policing plan stokes privacy concerns
content:
BRUSSELS — Senior EU officials warn that a sweeping new plan to arm the bloc’s police agency, Europol, for the AI era could threaten Europeans’ privacy.

As cybercriminals, terrorists and spies weaponize artificial intelligence for scams, extortion and cyberattacks, Brussels is betting on expanding Europol’s AI powers — the agency that has coordinated European police intelligence since 1998 — to help combat the risks.

“Europol is at a turning point,” said centrist European Parliament member Fabienne Keller, who serves on the justice and civil liberties committee. While “we need a stronger Europol, with the resources and capabilities to effectively support national law enforcement authorities,” Keller said. That “must go hand-in-hand with strong democratic oversight and robust safeguards for fundamental rights and data protection.”

Plans for a “transformative evolution” of the The Hague-based agency, announced this summer, would double its budget to €3 billion and give Europol a hands-on role in fighting new threats, with access to more data and advanced technology.

title: Musiikin käyttö vaalikampanjassa – tarvitsetko luvan?
content:
Miten ehdokkaat saavat käyttää musiikkia vaalikampanjoidensa tilaisuuksissa tai vaalivideoissa? Mitä tarkoitetaan musiikin käytön poliittisella yhteydellä? Kertaamme musiikin poliittisen käytön periaatteet.

Jos haluat käyttää musiikkia vaalikampanjassasi tai muussa poliittisessa yhteydessä, sinun tulee pyytää lupaa sekä kotimaisen että ulkomaisen musiikin käyttöön suoraan musiikin tekijöiltä tai heidän kustantajiltaan. Samalla voit sopia myös mahdollisesta musiikin käytön korvauksesta, jonka musiikin tekijä tai hänen kustantajansa sinulta laskuttaa.

Musiikin käyttö poliittisessa yhteydessä kuuluu tekijän itsensä hallinnoimiin taloudellisiin oikeuksiin. Siihen voivat liittyä myös respektioikeudet (moraalinen oikeus), jotka säilyvät aina tekijällä itsellään.

Tekijällä – tai hänen kustantajallaan, jos tekijä on kustantajansa kanssa niin sopinut – on oikeus päättää, millaisiin poliittisiin ajattelutapoihin, periaatteisiin ja tavoitteisiin hänen musiikkinsa yhdistetään.

title: Optogenetics wins the Nobel – one neuroscience breakthrough in a line of technological innovations helping scientists map and control the brain
content:
The brain is unbelievably complicated, which is both daunting and fascinating for neuroscientists like me. In the space of a cubic millimeter – about the size of a single poppy seed – there are tens of thousands of neurons and other brain support cells, all influencing each other’s function.

How do neuroscientists make sense of this complexity? And how did they get to the point where they could simply shine different colors of light on the brain to control neuron activity?

The answer is one step at a time, with a lot of help from technology.

Revisiting some of the technological advances that have supported researchers’ current understanding of how the brain works can point to where the field of neuroscience might be going next. There is a rough pattern to the technological advances that have led neuroscience to the present day: visualize the brain, measure its function and then control it.

Using light to influence neuronal function, known as optogenetics, allows neuroscientists to manipulate what neurons do millisecond by millisecond. The researchers whose work led to this technique won the 2026 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine.

title: Brazil election: Authoritarian right gain an edge, fueled by voter apathy and discontent
content:
The far-right bubble that has seen populist rightist figures elected across Latin America spilled over and flooded the ballot box in Brazil’s general elections held on Oct. 4, 2026 – fueled by a discontented and distrustful public. In spite of voting being mandatory in the country for literate citizens aged 18 to 70, a wave of disengagement swept across 33.4 million voters who did not cast a ballot — 21% of the electorate.

It was the highest abstention rate since 1998. We still need to investigate what produces bubbles and waves in contemporary politics, but I have a few tentative hypotheses about this process.

This kind of ebb and flow has three dimensions: affective, value-based, and political-ideological. The affective dimension is one of depressive sentiments. Three feelings predominate: resentment, anger and political fatigue. Anger stems from the fear of losing what one has and from the aversion generated by feeling neglected by the political leadership in power. Under affective polarization, it turns into hatred.

title: atNorth rakentaa uuden datakeskuksen Saloon
content:
Pohjoismaiden johtava suuren tehotiheyden colocation- ja räätälöityjen datakeskusratkaisujen tarjoaja atNorth rakentaa uuden FIN05-datakeskuksen Saloon. Hanke on osa yhtiön vastausta vastuullisen, korkean teholuokan digitaalisen infrastruktuurin kysyntään.

Salo soveltuu rakennuspaikkana hyvin kriittiselle infrastruktuurille, joka palvelee asiakkaita, joille luotettavat verkkoyhteydet ja korkea toimintavarmuus ovat keskeisiä vaatimuksia. Helsingin läheisyys ja suomalaisten teknologia-alan osaajien saatavuus tukevat hankkeen toteutusta.

FIN05 rakennetaan 28,6 hehtaarin maa-alueelle. Ensimmäisen vaiheen 75 MW:n sähköntarve on varmistettu ja koko hankkeen 230 MW:n sähköntarpeen edellyttämät ratkaisut kartoitettu. Kohde kytketään kantaverkkoon Fingridin sähköaseman kautta.

atNorthin oman investoinnin Salon kohteeseen arvioidaan olevan noin 2 miljardia euroa. Arvio ei sisällä atNorthin asiakkaiden omistamia palvelimia eikä niiden asennusta, joihin asiakkaat voivat investoida lisäksi arviolta jopa 10 miljardia euroa.

title: How the Poet Mary Oliver was “Saved by the Beauty of the World”
content:
Filmmaker Sasha Waters wasn’t shy when asked at the National Book Festival about the legacy of her latest documentary subject, the poet Mary Oliver: “I think we’re going to think of her as the (Walt) Whitman of the 20th century.”

That’s an almost impossible standard, as Whitman became synonymous with the American spirit in the late 19th century with poems such as “I Hear America Singing,” “Song of Myself,” “O Captain! My Captain!” and “I Sing the Body Electric.” He has since become an iconic American personality of the age, along with the likes of Abraham Lincoln, Mark Twain and Frederick Douglass.

But Oliver, who adored Whitman’s work, won the Pulitzer Prize and the National Book Award for her rapturous odes to nature and our connection to it. She was adored about as much as any poet since Whitman when she died, at 83, in 2019.

title: Conservative plans to slash aid budget would ‘irreparably damage’ UK’s global credibility, charities say
content:
Party’s pledge to reduce aid budget from £9bn a year to £1bn to fund new prison places branded as ‘posturing’

Conservative plans to slash the aid budget by 90% would leave the UK unable to cover existing contributions to the UN and World Bank and “irreparably damage” Britain’s global credibility, several organisations and charities have told the Guardian.

In a series of announcements at the Tory party conference in Birmingham, Kemi Badenoch said that as prime minister she would reduce the aid budget from £9bn a year to £1bn, to part-fund 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales. The culture budget would also be slashed by £1bn a year to fund the plans.

title: Minä, luddiitti
content:
Olen viime aikoina ajatellut australialaisen kirjailijan Max Barryn vuonna 2020 julkaistua scifi-kertomusta Providence, jonka luin muutama vuosi sitten. Barryn kirjassa ihmiskunta käy tähtienvälistä sotaa vierasta sivilisaatiota vastaan. Tarina keskittyy neljään astronauttiin Providence-aluksen kyydissä sotaretkellä, joka voi ratkaista koko sodan ja pelastaa ihmiskunnan.

(Spoiler alert: Skippaa seuraavat kaksi kappaletta, jos et halua juonipaljastuksia.)

Juonen juju on se, että avaruusalus on varustettu erittäin kehittyneellä tekoälyllä. Niin kehittyneellä, että astronautit ovat mukana käytännössä sivustakatsojina, joiden ainoa tehtävä on tallentaa ja kertoa matkasta, tuottaa kontsaa kotirintamalle. Avaruusalus tekee omiaan, sen logiikka on matkustajille musta laatikko. Sodan kulkuun ja lopputulokseen ihmisillä ei lopulta ole minkäänlaista vaikutusta. Kirjan tarinan voi tulkita kahdella tapaa: joko niin, että ihmisen merkitys syntyy tarinoista, joita kerromme toisillemme. Tai sitten niin, ettei ihmisillä ole enää merkitystä.

title: Embedded Collective Governance and Firm Strategy: The Case of New Zealand’s Māori Advisory Committee: Economic Research Working Paper No. 101
content: Firms increasingly build competitive advantage on cultural resources whose value derives from collective meaning, yet existing institutions either remove those symbols from the market or fail to protect them in time. We study the concept of embedded collective governance (ECG) for the use of traditional cultural expression: a governance form that embeds culturally-informed community review directly within market access institutions. We argue that ECG operates through two channels. Screening regulates entry at the registration gate. Certification rewards cultural alignment at the renewal margin, generating a premium for trademarks that survive culturally informed community review. We test ECG at the trademark level and the portfolio level using New Zealand’s 2003 Trademarks Act, which placed a Māori Advisory Committee (MAC) within the trademark system. Results confirm both channels: Māori related trademarks are less likely to be registered and expire in New Zealand relative to abroad. title: 10 Creative Ways Museums Can Use Food to Connect with Audiences
content:
Incorporating food into museum programming offers a unique and dynamic way to engage audiences by connecting cultural heritage, history, and art through a universal human experience. Here are ten innovative strategies, each illustrated by institutions that have successfully implemented them:

Themed supper clubs offer immersive dining experiences inspired by museum exhibitions. The Garden Museum in London has organized supper clubs featuring menus crafted around specific exhibitions, blending culinary arts with storytelling to create unforgettable evenings.

Workshops teaching traditional cooking methods can transform museums into living history centers. The Food Museum in Suffolk, UK, runs seasonal classes where participants learn to make dishes like Christmas mince pies, offering hands-on insights into culinary traditions.

Exhibitions dedicated to food can explore its cultural, historical, and social significance. The Southern Food & Beverage Museum in New Orleans showcases the culinary traditions of the American South, illustrating how food shapes cultural identity through historical artifacts and multimedia displays.

title: arXiv Is Rate Limiting Submissions Because It Can’t Keep up With AI Slop
content:
arXiv, an open-access repository where researchers publish preprint academic research, has announced it will rate limit submissions because it has been inundated with AI-written papers. A researcher can now only send in two pieces per calendar month and have a total of three active submissions at any given time. In a blog post about the change, arXiv said AI has made it too easy to spam the publisher’s inbox and its volunteer moderation team is overwhelmed.

“The heart of arXiv’s process for detecting and rejecting low-quality papers is our many volunteer moderators,” Thomas Dietterich, an Oregon State University professor emeritus and the chair of arXiv’s editorial advisory council said in a statement. “We are so grateful that they donate their time and expertise every day. However, a relatively small proportion of authors are submitting a large number of low-quality papers and consuming a disproportionate fraction of the moderators’ time. This is unfair to authors who continue to submit quality papers — their papers can be delayed for days or weeks as a result.”

Tutkijat, taiteilijat, journalistit ja muut asiantuntijat keskustelevat siitä, mikä saa ihmiset vaikenemaan ja millaiset rakenteet vaikuttavat siihen, ketkä pääsevät yhteiskunnassa ääneen.

Sanan- ja ilmaisunvapaus ovat tutkijoiden, taiteilijoiden ja toimittajien työn keskeisiä edellytyksiä. Heidän työnsä perustuu mahdollisuuteen tuottaa, tulkita ja jakaa tietoa, ajatuksia ja näkökulmia vapaasti myös silloin, kun ne haastavat totuttuja käsityksiä tai herättävät yhteiskunnallista keskustelua.

Kertomuksia hiljaisuudesta -lavaohjelmissa kuullaan kokemuksia ilmaisunvapauden merkityksestä ja siihen kohdistuvista paineista tutkimuksen, taiteen ja journalismin kentillä. Esiin nousevat vaikeat ja vaietut aiheet sekä kysymys siitä, keiden ääni yhteiskunnassa kuuluu ja kuka jää kuulematta.

title: Russia Attacks – Would NATO Freeze?
content:
Would NATO fight if Russia entered its territory? Yes, says CEPA Fellow Skip Davis, but it’s also the case that alliance readiness has been increased across the eastern flank in the last decade and now extends far beyond the ability to meet an armed attack.

Question: What would happen on the ground if Russian troops crossed into NATO territory? Would alliance commanders need to await permission to engage?

Davis: NATO forward land forces are multinational battle groups and brigades stationed on the eastern flank, mostly in countries bordering Russia. They have a lead nation, but they’re established in nine different countries along the east, from Finland all the way down to Romania, all the Baltics, Poland and Slovakia, Hungary. Under NATO doctrine, they have the right to respond in self-defense. They would not need permission to respond.

But that is the simplest response. We have to peel the onion a little bit because Russia would normally be expected to do some type of preparation.
